comparison_scope: Same six buildings, same actual representative days per building, same 2017 retained complete-day observations.
Weights calibrated on the same year; descriptive internal compression, not temporal holdout or unseen-site prediction.
All six candidates plotted, including peak-rejected cases2/5 and Genoveva whose maximum quantile error increases from61.913245891997846% to76.39741709111594%.
Observed-energy exclusion ranges4.586556475272855% to34.7855375071981%; improvements only apply to retained observations.
LP success and statistical adoption do not prove investment, capacity, comfort, physical operation or Chinese three-city field validation.

comparison_scope: Same two48m2 ideal-reference buildings, same continuous2880h Wuhan weather and TOU inputs,1h step, initial/terminal20C, comfort20..27C.
A heat-loss coefficient0.1043kW/K and capacity0.535576kWh/K fixed; B coefficient0.15645kW/K fixed, capacity changes0.535576 to2.142304kWh/K.
Only B heat capacity and shared electric cap axes vary; same fixed assets, zero free investment.
Increasing heat capacity lowers energy charge but increases electricity and fixed-factor CO2 in both cap settings; do not call it universal energy saving or peak reduction.
Shared cap decreases the heat-capacity cost saving by150.5231939521791yuan.
CO2 uses the registered constant0.4044kg/kWh factor and is redundant with electricity; it is not an independently varying environmental outcome.
Charges cover operating electricity energy only, not real engineering capital or lifecycle cost. Optimality is within the supplied finite model and solver tolerance.
